title: Implement materializers, drift, and repair
description:
Move every materialization producer — default rule family and generated fragments, default schemas, configured project projections, profile assets and static managed regions — into `repository_state`, and implement drift comparison and ownership-safe transactional repair over one final repository view. This builds on the typed mutation, audit, and claim synchronization already landed on main.

## Background

Default schema refresh, default rule membership, project rendering, and profile region rendering are today implemented in command-local and validation-resident helpers with separate byte renderers. This package makes `repository_state` the sole owner of the derive/compare pipeline and gives `jit validate --fix` one ownership-safe repair delta, so persisted derived state can never become a second source of truth.

## What to build

- One-way state pipeline: `repository_state::derive_materializations(image, declarations, seed, intent)` directly invokes the fixed materialization functions and returns sorted expected claims plus a deterministic exact delta; `repository_state::compare_materializations(image, expected)` returns typed drift; validation then evaluates an overlay of that delta. Derivation/comparison never call validation, and validation owns no alternate default/schema/projection/marker renderer. Semantic-mutation intent always invokes the complete producer set — callers cannot select default schemas but omit rule membership or projections. Render-only and repair intents are constrained complete operations, not arbitrary producer switches.
- Producer relocation (implementations, not aliases): move default family derivation, generated default-fragment serialization, default schema rendering, projection body/target rendering, target composition, and derive/compare from `validation::defaults`, `validation::serialize`, `validation::project_render`, `validation::projection`, and the repository projection helpers into `repository_state`. Validation retains rule execution/reporting and whole-repository policy checks but imports these final producers. `jit project render` composes every selected claim by safe target and deterministic producer order — shared-target composition is deterministic, never last-writer-wins — validates the complete overlay, and publishes once through the storage capability; the command-local pending-byte map, per-target writer, and partial publication loop are removed while the command-specific report stays stable.
- Managed-document reuse: profile/static managed regions and registry-driven projections reuse the one strict marker parser and splice primitive from the shared engine while retaining configuration-specific placement and rendering policies. Malformed, duplicate, crossing, or otherwise ambiguous markers fail before publication; well-formed nested regions remain supported; non-managed prose stays byte-for-byte unchanged. The intentionally nested dogfood guidance/invariants regions remain valid.
- Drift diagnosis and transactional repair: expected derived state is always recomputed from declared authorities — never read back from persisted bytes. Validation emits deterministic errors for missing, stale, or unexpected explicitly owned materializations while effective rules remain declaration-derived. `jit validate --fix` asks the same planner for one repair delta, applies it through the shared storage capability, reruns validation, and obeys the repair ownership-source matrix: it never rewrites an authored boundary it cannot prove; authored rule content (custom rows, comments/header/order, editable policy) is preserved unconditionally; ambiguous ownership is a non-repairable error, never a whole-file fallback rewrite; obsolete schema files are deleted only when a persisted default-rule reference or recorded producer ownership proves generation (filename convention alone is insufficient); profile asset/region repair happens only when the exact applied package/version/hash and provenance prove ownership.

Distilled §2 contracts: one-way state pipeline, exact declaration/producer disposition (materialization relocation), managed-document composition, and the repair ownership-source matrix. See `dev/active/cdc840ad-plan.md` §2 and plan decisions D2, D7, D8 for full detail. This upholds `@/inv/single-source-prose` — declared registries/config stay authoritative; derived materializations never override their sources.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every materialization derives from declared authority and composes shared targets deterministically.
- [hard] REQ-02: Drift/fix and authored-content preservation pass targeted plus full cumulative backend tests without a second renderer.

## Constraints

- Invoker-approved delivery model (2026-07-19): cumulative final-form wave commits land directly on `main`. The retired `integration/cdc840ad` branch is not authoritative and no integration-only final transition is required. Each commit runs targeted tests plus all prior cumulative package tests on both backends.
- No adapter, feature flag, compatibility re-export, dual path, temporary API, or second/alternate renderer. Producers are relocated implementations, not aliases; no old producer definition, re-export, wrapper, provider list, or callback hook remains.
- Repair uses declared sources and existing ownership records only — never a new compatibility inventory.
- Out of scope (plan D19/D20): lease credential/claim-log/claim-command redesign and worktree/data-root binding redesign.

Blast radius: default/schema/projection/profile producers, validation comparison and fix, and ownership-matrix tests.
